title: What limits a method at 359 patients and 113 events

a_capacity_against_noise.description: a ridge Cox fitted to pure noise and scored in sample

values.note: an oracle arm fitted IN-SAMPLE on the held-out fold at matched capacity (d principal components of the training fold's own basis), against a null at the same capacity.
values.corrected_null_definition: fit the permuted outcome, score THAT SAME permutation. Zero signal, identical n, event count, censoring and capacity. 200 draws per fold.
values.first_control_definition: fit the permuted outcome, score the REAL one. 1,000 draws. THIS WAS THE WRONG CONTROL and its answer was reported as a finding before the correction.
values.reading: a Cox fit to PURE NOISE, scored in-sample at d=16, reaches 0.7474. The real excess over a matched null is +0.0192 at d=16 and SHRINKS as capacity grows, which is what added noise dimensions look like.
values.withdrawn: the earlier reading -- that the image representation holds 0.2686 above its control and gives up 0.1170 to estimation -- is withdrawn. Both were artifacts of comparing an inflated quantity against an honest one.

b_weight_sweep.description: the 21-point weight sweep, the held-out-fold oracle and equal weighting

gated_fusion_oracle.which_baseline: the +0.0224 in the ledger is measured against the LINEAR fusion oracle (0.7268), not against the deployed equal weight (0.7191). Writing it without saying which would let a reader attach the smaller gain to the larger claim; both are recorded here because a self-consistency check on this file caught exactly that ambiguity.

values.reading: even given the held-out outcomes, the best fixed linear fusion gains +0.008 over the equal weight already in use, and the sweep's maximum sits exactly at equal weight. The room is not in the fusion rule.

c_gated_component_and_control.description: the gated component against its permuted-stratum control

values.note: the gating weights here are read off the SAME pooled outcome they are scored on, so this is an oracle-flavoured reference for whether gating is worth building in-fold, not an arm. Its control says how much the structure alone buys.

d_power.description: power against a true difference at this cohort's patient-resampling standard error

values.reading: a two-sided test at this cohort's SE detects a margin of about 0.059 at 80% power. The nine published entries on this benchmark span 0.596 to 0.691 and consecutive entries differ by 0.002 to 0.012, so almost none of the published ORDERING is resolvable at this n -- a statement about the benchmark, not about any one method.

e_competitor_across_seeds.description: the competitor arms as seed-averaged scores

values.construction: per seed 0-4: fit, score out-of-fold, percentile-normalise within fold. Then average the five score vectors and re-normalise within fold. Both sides of every comparison get this identical treatment.
values.not_the_primary_metric: the pre-registered primary is 0.7212, the MEAN OF FIVE PER-SEED CONCORDANCES. This table's 'ours' is the concordance of the AVERAGED SCORE, which is a different and slightly higher quantity. Averaging favours the competitor if anything: its seeds are full retrainings, ours are inner-CV partitions.

f_checkpoint_convention.description: PIBD at its best-validation checkpoint and at its final epoch
